title: InvoiceFlow — choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Confirmation Slip (a world of SWIFT/telex payment confirmations) as the direction to build. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Code-led: this is a working screen, it gets built, not comped.

options.label: Confirmation Slip
options.thesis: Every invoice decision printed as a settlement confirmation you can read line by line.
options.viewport: Deep ink-green rail carrying the queue as a ruled confirmation register; the selected invoice prints its audit lines into fixed cells.
options.risk: Mono collapses into terminal costume if the sans loses its job.

raised.raise: Live agent output cascades per character into fixed cells instead of fading in as a block.
A row whose status changes moves in place and holds a signal lamp until it is acknowledged.
The pipeline is drawn as a line bending only at 45° and 90°, with interchange nodes exactly where a human has to take over.

options.label: Audit Working Papers
options.lineage: public-accounting working papers and tick-mark notation
options.thesis: Each invoice is a working paper whose margin ticks are the evidence.
options.viewport: Buff ruled sheet with a margin column of drawn tick marks, one per validation rule, each opening into its own reasoning.
options.risk: The most familiar move for an audit product — the comfort of the obvious.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: The queue as a departure board: fixed columns, characters that clack into place.
options.viewport: Steel-framed board of fixed columns; the newest invoice flips character by character while everything else holds still.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: dense ruled rows that update in place. Loses on warmth across an eight-hour shift.
options.risk: Reads as signage when the reasoning prose has nowhere to sit.

options.label: Boarding Pass + Gate Board
options.lineage: airline boarding documents and gate boards
options.thesis: Invoice as a segmented pass; the queue as a board that reranks itself in place.
options.viewport: Board of flights-like rows ranked by arrival time; the selected invoice opens as a pass split into labelled segments.
options.case: Tabular figures and in-place reranking suit a live queue; gives the reasoning prose less room.
options.risk: One alert colour is a thin skin for five rule types.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.thesis: The pipeline as a line: stations are stages, interchanges are human handoffs.
options.viewport: Dark enamel panel with one line running the width; every invoice is a marker travelling it, stopped at the station that claimed it.
options.case: Explains flow at a glance and makes stalls legible; the map can outshout the invoice itself.
options.risk: Diagram-first screens make a clerk read a metaphor before the data.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.case: Fuses poorly: software-manual retrieval is not the clerk's mental model.
options.kept: Ply discipline — only the top layer carries emphasis, and a stepped rail encodes extent.
options.risk: Nostalgia for a manual nobody ever enjoyed using.

options.label: Metro Typographic Tiles
options.case: Fuses poorly: giant cropped type fights density in a queue screen.
options.kept: Colour fields own whole regions instead of sprinkling accents.
options.risk: A poster pretending to be a tool.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.case: Fuses poorly: playfulness is on the user's list of wrong outcomes.
options.kept: Every record carries fixed furniture — name, date, one-line note.
options.risk: Cute in a screenshot, exhausting in a shift.

canonCard.label: The admin-SaaS standard
canonCard.thesis: White ground, blue accent, sidebar, four stat cards — executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar navigation, KPI cards across the top, a table below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every AP dashboard by design.
